label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_rpg.mdl, models/w_hgun.mdl, models/w_suit.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, C, B, A where the asset was D, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Against the brief's words (a waist-high control console with dials, two screens and a row of switches), the outline is right: a closed box about 40 high with a flat top slab overhanging all round, and the controls on the front face. Side and back views show no part sticking out beyond what a console would have. Small nubs on the lower sides and base tabs seen in the side and below views are minor and do not change the silhouette.

M2.reason: Measured: 66 long by 31.8 deep by 40 high. The brief's 40 for height is matched exactly (sizeOff 0).

M3.reason: Dials and screens are present: five dials in a row on the front, and two screens. The switches are the weak part. The row is a line of about six small dark squares along the top of the front face (front and front-left views), read as recesses at game size, not as switches. The dials are plain white domes with no pointer or scale, so they read as knobs. The two side stubs are not in the brief.

M4.reason: The body is grey-green painted steel, the top a lighter grey cap, the screens dark glass-green, the dials pale metal. Each region reads as the material the brief implies (rusted steel, glass, metal) and they agree across the views.

M5.reason: The rust and panel texture on the sides and back is present. The two screens are flat dark green with no display, glow or lettering, and the dials carry no markings. Only the switch row is detailed, and at this scale it reads as blur. The brief asks for screens and dials, so this is clearly short of a console's surface detail.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rubric. The line-up test is measured apart and is not scored here. In lineup.png beside the rocket and the suit it reads as a Valve prop of its kind.

M7.reason: Front faces the viewer with the screens and dials on it, the box stands upright on a flat base in the side and front views, and the bottom is flat so it sits on its origin.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. 256 triangles against a median of 238 for Half-Life's props of its kind, far under twice the median. The underside, seen in the below view, is closed and flat. The dials and side stubs are attached to the body and float nowhere.
